name: graphify
description: Assimilate Graphify knowledge-graph capabilities into AgentOS through auditable Ouroboros plugin commands.

commands.name: build
commands.summary: Build or update a Graphify knowledge graph for a repo-bounded local path.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description: Repo-bounded local target path to graph.

commands.name: query
commands.summary: Query an existing Graphify graph and emit reusable evidence.

arguments.name: question
arguments.description: Question to answer from the graph.

commands.name: path
commands.summary: Return the shortest path between two graph concepts or nodes.

commands.name: explain
commands.summary: Explain a graph node and its important connections.

commands.name: add
commands.summary: Fetch a URL into a Graphify corpus after explicit network trust.

commands.name: serve
commands.summary: Start long-running Graphify MCP/watch surfaces only after explicit trust.

commands.name: neo4j-push
commands.summary: Push graph data to Neo4j only after explicit external-write trust.

capabilities.name: ledger
capabilities.reason: Record invocation intent, selected command, graph stats, and result summary.

capabilities.name: state
capabilities.reason: Persist graph build/query state and resumable metadata.

capabilities.name: provenance
capabilities.reason: Record input roots, generated artifacts, backend/model hints, and source evidence.

capabilities.name: handoff
capabilities.reason: Attach Graphify reports, graph JSON, and query outputs to downstream AgentOS workflows.

capabilities.name: progress
capabilities.reason: Surface extraction/chunking/build progress and blocked prerequisites.

capabilities.name: runtime
capabilities.reason: Launch the upstream graphify CLI in a bounded subprocess.

capabilities.name: mcp
capabilities.reason: Expose Graphify MCP stdio server only when explicitly trusted.

permissions.reason: Read target project, corpus files, and existing graph artifacts.
Write graphify-out, cache files, reports, graph files, wiki/Obsidian/export outputs, and handoffs.
Execute the upstream graphify command or python -m graphify.
Fetch URLs, clone GitHub repositories, or resolve remote resources when requested.
Call configured model APIs, push to Neo4j, or use external API-backed features when requested.
Support Graphify PR dashboard or PR impact analysis if enabled.
Start or expose the Graphify MCP server.
Push graph data to Neo4j; documented as a schema pressure point for richer future database scopes.
